column1: # Pinned dev toolchain, read by scripts/tools.sh (make tools).
# Columns (tab-separated): name  version  platform  url  sha256
# Rule: a pin is the newest stable release published at least 7 days before it was pinned
# (Renovate minimumReleaseAge). Pinned on 2026-11-20. The sha256 comes from the vendor's checksum
# file (helm: <asset>.sha256sum; node: SHASUMS256.txt; kind, kubeconform, ct, helm-unittest, actionlint,
# hadolint, gitleaks, oasdiff, cosign, kyverno: the release checksum file; uv: the <asset>.sha256 beside the asset; yq: the sha256 column of
# the release `checksums`). squawk and shellcheck publish no checksum file: their sha256 is the GitHub
# release-asset digest, confirmed against the downloaded bytes. bats is the GitHub tag archive (no
# vendor checksum exists), hashed on download; a changed archive is refused.
# The uv row comes first: scripts/tools.sh installs it to .tools/bin/uv, and every uv:<pkg> row below uses it.
# The backend image copies uv from the official image at the same version (a test keeps the two equal).
# Rows with url uv:<pkg> are Python tools. Each is installed into its own venv,
# .tools/uv-tools/<name>, with `uv pip install --require-hashes -r tools/requirements/<name>.txt`
# (every transitive dependency hash-pinned; `make pins-refresh` regenerates a lock in place with
# `uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-header --python-version 3.13 --python-platform x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
# plus `--exclude-newer` (now minus 7 days) and pyyaml held at the version in tools/requirements/pyyaml.txt),
# on the pinned `python` row.
# Their sha256 column is `-` because the hashes live in the requirements file. yamale and yamllint
# are what `ct lint` shells out to. `uv:python` runs `uv python install <version>` (uv's own cache);
# uv verifies that download with its built-in checksums, which is accepted here.
# Node: the Active LTS (26.x). This row is the one source: frontend/.nvmrc, frontend/.node-version, the builder
# images in Dockerfile.frontend and Dockerfile.nginx, the runtime image major, engines.node and packageManager
# (the npm bundled with this Node) are each locked to it by tests/supply_chain/test_frontend_image.py.
# Adding darwin-arm64: copy each linux-amd64 row, set platform to darwin-arm64, point the url at the
# vendor's darwin/arm64 asset, take its sha256 from the same vendor checksum file, and add the
# asset's executable path to the case in scripts/tools.sh if its layout differs.
# kubectl (bare binary from dl.k8s.io, sha256 from <binary>.sha256 beside it): must stay within one
# minor version of the cluster (the Kubernetes version-skew policy); change the pin when the cluster moves.
uv
# Helm major: see the default-helm line. Both majors are installed
# (helm3, helm4); `helm` links to the default.
#default-helm: 4
# Reason: with Helm 4.3.2 and 3.22.1 against the chart and no cluster, `helm lint`,
# `helm template | kubeconform -strict` (33 resources valid) and `helm unittest` pass on both majors,
# `ct lint` (before the values files were reformatted) exited 1 on both with byte-identical output, because of
# yamllint "braces" findings in the chart's values.yaml (a chart issue, not a Helm-major difference); it passes now. Helm 4 is the current line (and what the owner's
# machine runs), so the template targets it; helm3 stays installed to prove the chart still renders
# on 3.x. The helm3 pin only has to render the chart.
helm3
helm4
kubectl
kind
kubeconform
ct
helm-unittest
